correctness.rationale: The fixed-vector error is the quadratic form of E[B^T B] for chronological error transition B. In a word of rank-one projections the Gram matrix is the first projection times the squared overlaps of consecutive ranges. Summing separately the six label permutations and 27 IID words gives the reported difference and determinant exactly; the calculation was independently repeated symbolically with a rational parametrization covering s>0. The two projection lines span the plane. For u<1/2 the difference is positive definite, at u=1/2 it has rank one, and for 1/2<u<1 it is indefinite. The repeated-row normal gives the asserted negative IID-minus-RR gap there. The exact risks at (c,s)=(4/5,3/5) match, and the distinct-row RR-minus-IID gap is 155773981063185047/1754082541013512921875>0. Strict inequality also persists under perturbation by continuity. For two labels the difference is (1−u)(P+Q)/4; coincident projections give equality and with one label the two protocols coincide. This is one epoch with equal label probabilities, not sampling distinct row directions, multiepoch convergence, or a three-distinct-row classification. originality.rationale: Credit the sharp all-starting-vector Loewner boundary for this three-row family and its minimum label count, not exact IID MSE or the general distinction between reshuffling metrics. A later-dated catalogue result reproduces the normal-direction cutoff and exact counterexample and generalizes that direction in multiplicity, but does not cover the all-vector ordering. value.rationale: Sharp projective-angle and label-count boundaries resolve a focused version of a motivated sampler comparison. The example shows why operator-norm evidence cannot decide every fixed-vector mean-square comparison, even for a full-rank two-dimensional system and an epoch of only three projections. Perturbation to distinct directions shows this is not just an equality-degeneracy of duplicated observations. No broad sampler recommendation or long-run claim is inferred.
